title: Koszul-regular closed-immersion charts for an unramified lci morphism
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $u:Z\to Y$ a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Assume that $u$ is formally unramified in the square-zero test sense of [lem-sfb-space-universal-conormal], and is locally a complete intersection: on compatible etale scheme charts it locally factors as a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with ideal generated by a finite Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence], followed by a smooth morphism [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Then there are affine schemes $W_a,V_a$, etale maps $p_a:W_a\to Z$ and $q_a:V_a\to Y$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] with the $p_a$ jointly surjective, and closed immersions $i_a:W_a\hookrightarrow V_a$ satisfying $q_ai_a=up_a$, such that the ideal of each $i_a$ is generated by a finite Koszul-regular sequence. These charts may be chosen refining any given etale scheme covering of $Y$. Each $i_a$ remains locally cut out by a finite Koszul-regular sequence after any etale scheme base change on $V_a$.

source.place: Tag 06C5 (lemma-lci), with etale.tex Tag 04HH (lemma-unramified-etale-local), n=1, and more-morphisms.tex Tag 02HE (lemma-unramified-formally-unramified). Local complete intersections are locally of finite presentation; the chart construction is before the conormal calculation of Tag 06CB. Stability under etale refinement is divisors.tex Tag 067P (lemma-flat-base-change-regular-immersion), Koszul-regular clause.

proof.text: Fix an etale scheme covering $\{Y_b\to Y\}$ to be refined (use an atlas if none was prescribed). Pull it back to $Z$ and choose scheme atlases of the resulting spaces. The base-change and composition assertions of [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence] show that their maps to $Z$ form an etale covering. These schemes map to the corresponding $Y_b$. For each of their points choose an affine open $V_0\subseteq Y_b$ about its image and an affine open $U_0$ about the point inside the inverse image of $V_0$, using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Open inclusions are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], and composition gives compatible charts $a:U_0\to Z$, $b:V_0\to Y$ and $h:U_0\to V_0$. These $a$ jointly cover $Z$; each $b$ factors through a prescribed $Y_b$. The lci hypothesis supplies the local Koszul-regular/smooth factorizations of every $h$.

source.place: Tag 06C4 (definition-lci), compatible chart convention; spaces.tex Tag 02X2 and spaces-topologies.tex Tag 041F, atlas and covering base change.

proof.text: Each $h$ is locally of finite type. Indeed, near $x\in U_0$ take its assumed factorization $U\xrightarrow{j}P\xrightarrow{s}V_0$. Smoothness includes local finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Applying [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] at $j(x)$ gives affine opens $P_1=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $V_1=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $B$ finitely presented over $A$. The closed-immersion affine description [def-weil-closed-immersion] gives $j^{-1}(P_1)=\operatorname{Spec}(B/I)$. If $B=A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$, the images of the $t_i$ generate $B/I$ over $A$, whatever the ideal $I$ is. Thus every $x$ has an affine open neighbourhood $j^{-1}(P_1)$ mapping into the affine $V_1$ with finitely generated ring map, so $h$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] by the pointwise criterion [lem-weil-pbc-lft-pointwise-criterion]. The square-zero test of the hypothesis, over all scheme thickenings, contains the affine tests, so $u$ is formally unramified in the sense of [lem-sfb-space-formally-unramified-etale-charts]; by its clause (2), $h$ is formally unramified. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lft-formally-unramified-unramified] to conclude that $h$ is unramified. No finite generation of $I$ or Noetherian hypothesis was used.

source.place: Tag 02HE (lemma-unramified-formally-unramified), (2) implies (1); Tag 069F (definition-lci), factorization; spaces-more-morphisms.tex Tag 04G8.

proof.text: Fix $x\in U_0$, $y=h(x)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-etale-finite-neighbourhoods] to $h$ and the singleton list $x$. Obtain an etale neighbourhood $(T,t)\to(V_0,y)$ and finitely many opens $E_j\subset U_0\times_{V_0}T$, finite and unramified over $T$, with marked points $e_j$ unique over $t$ and purely inseparable residue extensions. There is a point of $U_0\times_{V_0}T$ over both $x$ and $t$: embed $\kappa(x)$ and $\kappa(t)$ over $\kappa(y)$ in a common field by [lem-weil-common-extension-fields]; the kernel of the induced map $\kappa(x)\otimes_{\kappa(y)}\kappa(t)\to M$ is prime, so [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points] gives such a point. The exhaustion clause of the finite-neighbourhood node says that this point is one of the $e_j$. In particular some marked $e_j$ maps to $x$.

source.place: Tag 04HH (lemma-unramified-etale-local), n=1: finite-neighbourhood construction before applying lemma-finite-unramified-one-point.

proof.text: For a marked $e_j$ mapping to $x$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-unramified-one-point-closed] applies to $E_j\to T$: finiteness, unramifiedness, uniqueness of the fibre point and pure inseparability were all supplied in Step 3. It gives an open $T^\circ\subseteq T$ containing $t$ such that $C=E_j\times_TT^\circ\to T^\circ$ is a closed immersion. The point $e_j$ survives. The map $C\to U_0$ is etale, since it is the restriction to an open of the base change of the etale map $T\to V_0$; use [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Composing with $U_0\to Z$ and $V_0\to Y$ gives compatible etale charts $C\to Z$, $T^\circ\to Y$ by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. Their closed immersion passes over $x$, and the target map still factors through the original $Y_b$.

Write $i:C\hookrightarrow T^\circ$ for the closed immersion of Step 4. Since this too is a compatible chart of $u$, the lci hypothesis gives, near every $c\in C$, a factorization $C_c\xrightarrow{j}P\xrightarrow{s}T^\circ$ with $j$ Koszul-regular and $s$ smooth. Compare the immersions $j$ and $i|_{C_c}$ over $T^\circ$ using [lem-sfb-koszul-immersion-smooth-ambient-independence], with smooth ambients $P$ and $T^\circ$ itself. The identity of $T^\circ$ is smooth: it is locally finitely presented with zero generators and relations and every infinitesimal lifting problem has its specified structure map as a lift [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. The comparison proves that $i$ is Koszul-regular near $c$. As $c$ was arbitrary, $i$ is Koszul-regular everywhere. This uses independence of the ambient smooth scheme, rather than assuming that the new closed-immersion charts already have regular ideals.

source.place: Tag 06C5 (lemma-lci), reduced to schemes; more-morphisms.tex Tags 069G (lemma-lci) and 069E (lemma-koszul-independence-factorization).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-koszul-closed-immersion-affine-criterion] at the chosen $e_j\in C$. It gives an affine open $V_a=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq T^\circ$ containing $i(e_j)$ such that $W_a=i^{-1}(V_a)=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ and $I$ is generated by a finite Koszul-regular sequence. Thus $i_a:W_a\hookrightarrow V_a$ is closed with the asserted global generators. Its maps $p_a:W_a\to Z$ and $q_a:V_a\to Y$ are etale by open restriction and composition [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation, lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence], and $q_ai_a=up_a$ because all restrictions came from the same chart square. The marked point remains and maps to $x$. Perform this construction for every point of the covering charts $U_0$; their point sets and the chosen data are sets in the fixed universes, so this yields a set-indexed jointly surjective family $\{p_a\}$. Every $q_a$ factors through its original $Y_b$, proving the refinement assertion. For $Z=\varnothing$ take the empty family.

source.place: Tag 063G (lemma-regular-ideal-sheaf-scheme), Koszul-regular clause; target affine restriction after Tag 04HH.

proof.text: Finally let $V\prime\to V_a$ be any etale scheme map. It is flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. The flat-ascent assertion of [lem-sfb-koszul-immersion-flat-ascent-etale-descent] makes $W_a\times_{V_a}V\prime\to V\prime$ Koszul-regular. It is still a closed immersion: on each affine test this is the quotient by the extended ideal, by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The affine criterion [lem-sfb-koszul-closed-immersion-affine-criterion] now supplies local finite Koszul-regular generators on $V\prime$, as required. Flatness is used here; no claim of preservation under nonflat base change is made.

proof_origin.place: Tag 04HH (lemma-unramified-etale-local), followed by spaces-more-morphisms.tex Tag 06C5 via more-morphisms.tex Tag 069E, and divisors.tex Tags 063G and 067P.
